The single unbalanced zero-sum quadruple is 1+1+2=4. Both displayed lower/upper deficits expand exactly to 3/2 and 45/14 and consist of nonnegative terms; their equality conditions force pure-mode minima and squared magnitudes (3,2,2) with phase lock at the maximum. The signed-count modulo-b argument proves nonresonance uniformly for b>=4, whereas b=3 exhibits explicit counterexamples. Independently checked exact polynomial deficit specializations and the package quartic-tensor checker; no reliance on finite samples for universal claims.
